subject: [hw] R1 findings F5/F7 (V02, LOW): 4 GiB fetch boundary; MMIO at guest address 0
body:
Two low-severity notes from the R1 review of DONE V02 rev 3 (emu/test_v02 PASS 830/830; core/mem read line by line; no other V02 finding).

F5 (emu/n2a32_core.c:509-526): the fetch does not bound pc+size to 4 GiB. At pc=0xFFFFFFFE with Thumb and a first halfword >= 0xE800, `memcpy(&hw2, c->mem->base + pc + 2, 2)` reads at base+0x100000000, one byte past the 4 GiB reservation. fault_handler only converts addresses inside [base, base+4GiB) to STOP_FAULT; a fault there is chained to the default action (host process death). On this host the adjacent mapping made the read succeed, so my repro observed STOP_UNDEF on garbage rather than a fault - either way the access is outside the reservation and the result is host-layout dependent. Suggested fix: before the fetch, if ((uint64_t)pc + size > 0x100000000ull) { c->stop=STOP_FAULT; c->stop_addr=pc; break; }. Same shape for the 16-bit fetch at pc=0xFFFFFFFF and for n2a32_ld32 at 0xFFFFFFFE. Repro file /tmp/n2hw-r1/edge.c (not in the tree).

F7 (emu/n2a32_mem.c:241-298): n2a32_mem_mmio() accepts addr=0, so the first megabyte can become readable MMIO while n2a32_ptr(0) is contractually NULL and n2a32_mem_map/protect reject address 0. No current caller maps 0; a one-line `addr == 0` rejection would keep the contract uniform.

No action needed on F5/F7 for the current integration; they are recorded in gpu/hwcodec/review/r1/FINDINGS.md and I will re-check if you change the code.
